messages:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a small, model-agnostic precision annotation plus a runtime "degradation_budget" so ops can trade quality for cost in a predictable way. TL;DR: annotate endpoints, not models.
mina: can you sketch the annotation shape? is this per-call or per-endpoint?
alex: per-endpoint by default, with per-call override. want it lightweight so SDKs can set/override. minimal fields: target_quality_loss_pct, preferred_bitpaths, fallback_policy.
jamal: +1 to per-endpoint default. worried about semantics of quality_loss_pct — how do we measure it?
rachel: we still use our eval hooks (prompt set fingerprints) for ground truth estimates, but runtime needs a quick proxy for SLO enforcement.
ajmal: suggestion: runtime enforces a conservative budget and emits a degradation_score per response. controllers can map that to tokens billed and trigger fallbacks.
alex: here's a tiny example schema I prototyped:
```json
{
  "precision_profile": {
    "target_quality_loss_pct": 1.0,
    "preferred_bitpaths": ["fp8","int8","int4"],
    "fallback_policy": "degrade_then-fallback_to_fp16",
    "max_inflight_lowbit_ratio": 0.25
  }
}
```
mina: that helps. how do we compute target_quality_loss_pct during onboard? do we require customers to run evals?
alex: ops: we surface a recommended delta from our benchmark bank; customers can accept recommended, run a quick shadow eval, or lock to conservative defaults.
ops-bot: CI reminder: there's an open PR that wires the profile into the runtime config: <https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/987>. Tests failing on one case.
jamal: runtime needs two things: (1) cheap, monotonic degradation metric (we already have degscore) and (2) admission control to respect max_inflight_lowbit_ratio to avoid tail latency spikes.
rachel: agree — also record per-token quality proxy and aggregate for alerting (we can reuse telemetry tags from the last rollout).
mina: migration question: existing endpoints have no profile. default behavior?
ajmal: default = conservative: preferred_bitpaths [fp16], target_quality_loss_pct = 0.  opt-in for any lowbit.
alex: ops UX: add console toggle with "auto-recommend" that runs quick shadow sampling and suggests profile. Quick wins for customers: 20–30% token cost saving on dense workloads with <=1% quality loss.
jamal: long-term: we should unify this with model metadata so model catalog advertises expected degcost curves per bitpath. then policy engine can do cost-aware routing.
rachel: and we need a small compatibility shim: when profile mentions bitpath that runtime doesn't support, fallback to nearest supported and annotate response with why.
mina: any perf concerns for routing? additional lookup latency?
ajmal: we can cache compiled decision trees per endpoint and invalidate on profile change. negligible cost.
alex: next steps: (1) update RFC doc with the schema + migration plan, (2) add a lightweight SDK surface for per-call override, (3) patch the runtime admission controller PR (ops PR link above). I'll update RFC by EOD.
mina: sounds good. if someone can open a small spike to shadow-eval the recommended defaults that'd be helpful — volunteer?
jamal: I'll take the spike, will use two LLM families and the canonical prompt sets.
rachel: awesome. ping me on the PR for telemetry naming.
ops-bot: Scheduled: run-spike-job #482 queued (ETA ~2h).
alex: thanks everyone — will post updated RFC link here when done. :thumbsup:
